pages.text: A sealed room has $(bold)one temperature$(). Heaters, connected Cores and fires all warm the same air and walls.

pages.title: One Reading
pages.text: The thermostat and HUD use that reading. Walking toward a Core or campfire adds nothing.$(br2)Your gear and effects still adjust your HUD.

pages.title: Air and Walls
pages.text: Heaters warm the air, the air warms the walls, the walls lose heat outward.$(br2)After shutdown, stored heat cools gradually.

pages.title: Warm-up
pages.text: Warm-up takes far more power than Holding.$(br2)More or stronger heaters speed it up, at the same target.

pages.title: Target
pages.text: Heaters default to $(bold)20°C$(); a $(l:heating/thermostat)Thermostat$(/l) picks 10-30°C.$(br2)Passive heat can overshoot. Cut it or open a $(l:heating/heat_vent)Heat Vent$(/l).

pages.title: Fuel Estimates
pages.text: Holding 8% means about 8% of full burn rate, averaged over a few seconds. Time left is an estimate.
Warm-up, target, insulation, weather and breaches change demand; machinery and frostmites add cost.$(br2)Judge by the fuel you load. There is no fixed wool-to-glass ratio.

pages.title: After a Breach
pages.text: A $(l:heating/atmospheric_breach)breach$(/l) removes the air; the walls keep their heat.$(br2)Reseal and restore oxygen, and the new air warms from them.
Without air, burners heat walls less, and radiant warmth only partly protects you.$(br2)Atmosphere restored means air, not warmth. A thermostat cuts heating; it can't cool.
